title: Enhance Diffusion to Improve Robust Generalization

problem.claim: Adversarially trained neural networks struggle to generalize robustly and suffer from substantial overfitting.

gap.claim: AT research lacks consensus on hyperparameter settings with performance guarantees, and customized settings impede fair comparison between model designs.

contributions.claim: The paper approximates PGD-AT dynamics with a continuous-time stochastic differential equation and identifies the diffusion term as determining robust generalization.
The analysis indicates that robust generalization is positively correlated with the ratio between learning rate and batch size.
The paper proposes Diffusion Enhanced Adversarial Training (DEAT) to manipulate the diffusion term with virtually no extra computational burden.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DEAT as a novel approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors theoretically report that DEAT achieves a tighter generalization bound than PGD-AT.
The authors report an extensive empirical investigation in which DEAT universally outperforms PGD-AT by a significant margin.

narrative_sequence.summary: Adversarial perturbations threaten deep neural networks, while adversarial training is presented as a strong defense.
The paper targets hyperparameter-setting and robust-generalization problems in adversarial training.
For PGD-AT, the authors use an SDE approximation to connect the diffusion term with robust generalization and derive a learning-rate-to-batch-size implication.
The authors propose DEAT to manipulate diffusion with virtually no additional computational burden.
The abstract reports tighter theoretical bounds and favorable empirical comparisons against PGD-AT.

source_observation.claim: The diffusion term in the SDE approximation is reported to determine robust generalization, with robust generalization positively correlated with the learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio.

interpretation.claim: Optimization noise and training-scale choices may be useful control variables for robust generalization.

application.claim: When designing adversarial training procedures, analyze and tune diffusion-related effects rather than treating learning rate and batch size as unrelated settings.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this relationship holds beyond the PGD-AT framework or under settings not studied in the paper.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the hyperparameter performance guarantee, datasets, architectures, attack configurations, evaluation metrics, or numerical margins.
The abstract does not provide details of the DEAT algorithm or its theoretical assumptions.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported theoretical or empirical claims.
